summary: Arghyadip Mondal specializes in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. Attested in 2026, he was a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972) and taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.

Arindam Chakrabarti, a scholar in philosophy and Indology, earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford. He taught at Delhi, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (Professor attested 2009–2014, Emeritus attested 2026), and Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
Aritri Dutta works in Tibetology and religious studies. As an external PhD student attested in 2026, she studied at Leiden University under the supervision of Henk Blezer.

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Harvard and Leiden (PhD ~2000–2004 under Henk Bodewitz), and held posts at Groningen, the Kern Institute, Leiden University, and École française d'Extrême-Orient (Prof. 2008).

Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval was a linguist and scholar. He was appointed professor of modern Arabic at INALCO in 1821 and professor of Arabic at the Collège de France in 1833, joining the Académie des Inscriptions in 1849.

Arnold J. Toynbee was a historian who studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He was a fellow of Balliol College and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1888/1899–1926).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, worked for the Colonial Office (~1901–1914), and served as a professor at the University of Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

Arthur Christensen was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1903) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair in Oriental studies (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London (~1857–1860). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880) and examined Sanskrit manuscripts for the Chief Commissioner of Mysore in 1870.
Arthur Evans was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Harrow School (~1865–1870) and Brasenose College, Oxford (1870), and he later taught John Marshall.
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright was a historian and scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard, he taught at Stanford (1947–1959) and became the Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He served as Professor at SOAS and the University of London, and later headed the Asian Civilizations department at Australian National University (~1965–1978).

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), studying under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Pari Sangye.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena, where he earned his doctorate in 1813. His teachers included Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf, and he held a lectureship in Berlin in 1820.
